bullets: Drainage is the single highest-leverage design choice on any trail — ignoring it means rebuilding the trail from scratch a year later.
The most common mistake new builders make is grading too aggressively; internalizing this makes the rest of the design decisions easier.
Bench cuts on hillsides aren't optional — the shortcut on day one becomes the washout on year three.
Soil structure matters more than people think, a pattern observed holding across three different teams.
Land-stewardship conversations have to happen before the first dig rather than after — the framing reveals which trade-offs a project is making.
The machine-built versus hand-built trails question is a position that has been revised over time rather than settled at the outset.
Second-order effects of trail design choices are the part most people miss, and failure modes are harder to spot outside well-established tooling.
Picking one idea and running it for two weeks is the recommended starting point — the rest is iteration.
